clue.text: Lecturer parks jeep without bumpers badly

indicators.note: letters arranged badly are out of their proper order and must be put right
a vehicle's bumpers sit at its front and back, so the word loses its two end letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before it loses its ends

explanation.surface: A careless lecturer leaves a battered jeep with its bumpers missing in the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the jeep to EE, add PARKS, and rearrange PARKSEE into SPEAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives a talk or address to an audience is a public speaker.

indicators.note: the hairdo is holding the next word inside it, like hands round an object

parts.note: a perm is a permanent-wave hairstyle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A salon customer's hairdo is being prepared for a stage appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a piece of music or a role is to perform it for an audience.

clue.text: Military official at home once more

parts.note: an aga or agha was an Ottoman military commander
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A senior army officer is back at home once more after a posting.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga is an old Turkish title for a military officer, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Again and once more are synonyms, both meaning another time or repeatedly.

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can be rearranged
without tells us to take away the letters of the little word his from the long word

parts.note: taken as written
the three letters removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: Someone has shed the cheesiness that used to cling to him and now has a liberated spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, I and S out of CHEESINESS to leave CEENESS, which rearranges to ESSENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit of something is its essential nature, its essence; an essence is also a concentrated extract.

parts.note: surface reading: a bird belonging to the lecturer in the first answer
setter's reading: a kind of loudspeaker named after birdsong, since it handles the highest notes

explanation.walkthrough: The first answer is a loudspeaker; the high-frequency unit in a speaker cabinet is named for the sound a small bird makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker unit for high frequencies, and anything that chirps like a songbird tweets.

parts.note: surface reading: a pet dog belonging to the lecturer in the first answer
setter's reading: a kind of loudspeaker named after a dog's bark, since it handles the lowest notes

explanation.walkthrough: The first answer is a loudspeaker; the bass unit in a speaker cabinet is named for the deep noise a dog makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woofer is a large loudspeaker unit for low frequencies, and a barking dog goes woof.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: performing or putting a plan into effect
second meaning: putting someone to death as a legal punishment

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests carrying a body away; the two phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both accomplishing a task and putting a condemned person to death.

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
ample means plenty, more than enough

explanation.surface: A fashion model is old enough to work, or a mature model is quite enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to be copied is an example or exemplar to follow.

clue.text: Pen pals parted over shades of light and dark

indicators.note: words turned over are tumbled about, so their letters come out in a new order

parts.note: all three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Two correspondents went their separate ways over a disagreement about colour shades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parted' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are needed in the fodder; 'over' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt-and-pepper describes hair or fabric speckled with a mix of white and dark grey tones.

indicators.note: only a part of the long word is wanted, a run of consecutive letters within it

parts.note: the run of letters just after the Shakespe- start

explanation.surface: A section of the Bard's range as a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a scope or field of activity, which is one sense of area, as in area of expertise.

clue.text: Cleaner works for Doctors, Casualty and General Hospital?

parts.note: soap is the commonest cleaner
opus means a work, and its plural is the word here

explanation.surface: A hospital cleaner works for the doctors and the casualty and general wards.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctors and Casualty are long-running British TV medical dramas; General Hospital is the American daytime one. The question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: All three are long-running serial television dramas, the genre named after the detergent makers who sponsored early ones.

clue.text: Terribly sad now dud shipment moved

indicators.note: a shipment that is moved gets shifted about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A disappointed trader is glum because a faulty consignment has just been delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone feeling low, gloomy and depressed, which is being terribly sad.

indicators.note: something lurking in a place is hidden inside it, so the biter goes within

parts.note: a boy is a son, and the 's adds the S
a midge is a tiny biting fly

explanation.surface: A biting insect is hiding in a boy's bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: SMIDGEON is a variant spelling of smidgen.
explanation.definitionFit: Smidgeons are tiny amounts, so they are little bits of something.

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the first word are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a fiend is a devil

explanation.surface: Study up on a demon, or on a reckless adventurer.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person who enjoys dangerous stunts, someone who takes risks.

clue.text: They say young person could be a gold-digger

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: a minor is someone under the age of majority

explanation.surface: Gossips say a youngster might be marrying for money.
explanation.walkthrough: A gold-digger usually means someone after a rich partner; here it is literally a person who digs for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs gold out of the ground is a kind of miner, so a gold-digger could be one.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the beginning point, as in going back to square one
second meaning: a sudden jerk of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a board game instruction; the phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the beginning of something and a sudden involuntary jerk, as in giving someone a start.

parts.note: a net is a trap for catching things

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the words and spell what we hear

parts.note: ease spoken, then spelt as the end of a circus word

explanation.surface: An acrobat swings above the safety net with practised ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes that circus acrobats swing on.

clue.text: After game soldiers in casualty say sorry

indicators.note: the game and soldiers sit in the casualty department, enclosed by it

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
polo is a game played on horseback
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: After a match, injured soldiers in the emergency ward apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the soldiers after the game; both then go inside A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret, which is to say sorry.

clue.text: Seafood best cooked in liquid, or roasted to begin with

indicators.note: the cooked word goes in, placed inside the initials
cooking changes something's form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Seafood is best cooked in liquid, or else roasted, to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' works on the initials, not the word liquid: the cooked letters go between the second and third initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large marine crustacean eaten as seafood.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: noticed or caught sight of
second meaning: covered in dots, like the dog breed's coat

explanation.walkthrough: A Dalmatian is a white dog with black dots, so 'as a Dalmatian' describes a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both noticed by someone and marked with dots, which is how a Dalmatian's coat looks.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
craps is a dice game

explanation.surface: Bits left over from a small game animal after a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are small leftover pieces of food after a meal, the remnants.

clue.text: Husband and I put lid on hamper

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
taken as written
a cap is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: A couple closes the lid on their picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket noun, but it is the verb meaning to obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder or impede them, which is to handicap them.

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Bambi is the fawn in the Disney film
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A young fawn mostly loves eating grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is botanically a giant woody member of the grass family.

clue.text: Heads in mafia racket bring in godfather as supremo

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Mafia bosses running a racket bring in the godfather as their overall chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Big is slang for the boss of a criminal organisation, the person in overall charge.

clue.text: An ever-changing man is a dangerous thing

indicators.note: letters that keep changing shift into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man who never stops changing is a dangerous thing to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in ever-changing hides the split: ever is fodder, changing the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve agent is a toxic chemical weapon attacking the nervous system, certainly something dangerous.

clue.text: A couple take part in placebo therapy

indicators.note: the letters wanted take only a part in the following words, a run spanning them

parts.note: the run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Two people volunteer for a trial of treatment with dummy pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refers to two things together, a pair or a couple of them.

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: words playing about are jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician is still performing after the church service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After church' puts the rearranged letters after CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so is a kind of instrumental musician.

clue.text: Macbeth may be back, for example with pictures — extremely dreary

indicators.note: back means read from the end towards the start

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
pictures are works of art

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A production of Macbeth may return with illustrations but be thoroughly dreary.
explanation.walkthrough: EG joined with ART is read backwards to give TRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, so it is an example of the genre.
